title: AI used to create virtual models of Canada’s 25 most wanted criminals

 The Canadian Press Published November 19, 2026 Updated 5 hours ago   Open this photo in gallery: The Bolo Program website displays AI models of Canada's 25 most wanted criminals, shown in this handout image, on Nov. 19. HO/The Canadian Press

   Police agencies from across Canada have used artificial intelligence to create virtual models of the country’s 25 most wanted criminals moving as they would in real life. 
 The AI models of the fugitives appeared crossing hands and moving their heads, wearing casual shirts or hoodies and pants, on a large screen at the Toronto police college while police announced the newest list in the Bolo Program.
 The national program encourages police and the public to help find the fugitives.
 Max Langlois, the program’s executive director, said it uses new ways every year to make sure people are on the lookout for the most wanted suspects on the list.
 “This year with the help of AI, as you can see, we bring our top 25 fugitives into this room life-sized, moving as they might if you saw them on the street, at the supermarket, at the airport or anywhere else,” he said.
 “If it feels uncomfortable, that’s the point.”
 Satinderjeet Singh, who is also known as Goldy Brar, topped this year’s list. He is wanted by Winnipeg police on a Canada-wide warrant for what police say was an “execution-style murder” of 39-year-old Sukhdool Singh Gill on Sept. 20, 2023.
 Winnipeg police deputy chief Cam Mackid said police are offering $250,000 for any information that leads to the arrest of 32-year-old Singh, who originally entered Canada on a student visa in 2017 and is now known to be a high-ranking member of the Lawrence Bishnoi Gang, which Canada designated a terrorist group.
 “This is an India-based transnational organized crime syndicate,” Mackid said. 
 “(Singh) is currently wanted on charges of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder.” 
 Mackid said Singh has lived in California and various parts of Canada and he is now wanted in India, Canada and the United States. 
 “(He) has been wanted for some time by Indian authorities for a murder that occurred in that country in 2022,” Mackid said
 “In July of this year, (he) was indicted by a U.S. federal grand jury in Los Angeles on numerous charges. And in September, he was added to the FBI’s 10 most wanted list with a substantial reward.”
 Kyle Douglas Prouse, who allegedly shot a security guard inside Fairview Mall in Toronto in April before fleeing the area, held the No. 2 spot on the list of Canada’s 25 most wanted suspects. 
 Police are offering a $100,000 reward for information leading to his arrest. 
 Toronto police Chief Myron Demkiw said Prouse has ties to Toronto and Vancouver and is believed to be armed and dangerous.
 Six of the top 25 most wanted fugitives have connections to Toronto, including Cody Rudifo, No. 3 on the list, who is wanted in the fatal shooting of 34-year-old Christopher Gordon last month in the Lawrence Heights area of the city, Demkiw said.
 “The Bolo Program has shown time and time again what happens when police and the public work together,” Demkiw said.
 “Since 2018, 19 of the 28 Toronto cases featured by Bolo have ended in an arrest, including the case that held last year’s No. 1 spot.”
 “Bolo” is a common term used by police forces that stands for “be on the lookout.”
